findings.title: resolve() expiry check is inverted — deletes valid links
findings.description: Condition `Clock::now() < expires_at` is true when the link has NOT yet expired, but the branch erases the link and returns false. Every valid resolve deletes the link; expired links fall through to increment hits and return the target. The comparison must be `>` (or `>=`).

findings.title: require_admin() uses || instead of && — always denies
findings.description: `session.role != "admin" || session.role != "owner"` is a tautology: any string is not equal to at least one of the two values, so every session is rejected including admins. The intent is to allow either role.

findings.title: last_code() returns dangling string_view to local
findings.description: `newest` is a local std::string destroyed on return; the returned string_view dangles and any use is undefined behavior.

findings.title: format_row() returns dangling pointer to stack array
findings.description: `row` is a local `char[128]`; returning `const char*` to it dangles on return. Callers reading the pointer get undefined behavior.

findings.title: check_targets() off-by-one reads past vector end
findings.description: Loop condition `i <= links.size()` allows `i == links.size()`, accessing `links[links.size()]` out of bounds. On an empty vector this crashes on the first iteration.

findings.title: page() end computed as size+1 causes out-of-range iterator
findings.description: When `offset+size` exceeds the collection, `end` is set to `all.size() + 1`, then `all.begin() + end` is past `all.end()`, which is undefined behavior in the range constructor.

findings.title: validate() always returns true even when problems found
findings.description: Problems are collected and logged but the function unconditionally returns true, so `main()` never fails startup on invalid config (e.g. port out of range).

findings.title: bearer_token() null-dereferences when header has no space
findings.description: If `header` contains no space (empty or malformed Authorization value), `strchr` returns nullptr and `space + 1` dereferences null, crashing.

findings.title: stats() divides by zero when store is empty
findings.description: `g_store->total_hits() / g_store->size()` divides by zero when no links exist, causing a crash (integer division) or floating-point exception depending on types.

findings.title: success_rate() integer division always yields 0 or 100
findings.description: `used / links_.size() * 100` performs integer division first; e.g. 3/4 == 0, so result is 0 unless every link was used. Same pattern in cache.cpp utilization().

findings.title: utilization() integer division always yields 0 or 100
findings.description: `entries_.size() / limit_ * 100` does integer division first; for any non-full cache the result is 0.

findings.title: rename() validates 'from' twice, never validates 'to'
findings.description: `validate_code(from)` is called twice; `to` is never validated, so an invalid destination code (wrong length or characters) is accepted.

findings.title: LINKD_TIMEOUT_MS treated as seconds — 1000x error
findings.description: Env var is documented as milliseconds but assigned as `Seconds{ms}` directly, making a 5000ms timeout become 5000 seconds.

findings.title: LINKD_CACHE_TTL_MS treated as seconds — 1000x error
findings.description: Same as timeout: millisecond env var assigned directly to Seconds.

findings.title: LINKD_FETCH_LIMIT parsed but never stored
findings.description: The parsed value is cast to void and discarded; `cfg.fetch_limit` keeps its default regardless of the env var.

findings.title: prune() iterator invalidation and returns wrong value
findings.description: Erasing via `links_.erase(it)` then `++it` in the for-loop increment uses an invalidated iterator (UB). Also returns `links_.size()` instead of `removed`, contradicting the doc comment.

findings.title: sweep() iterator invalidation on erase
findings.description: Same pattern as prune: `entries_.erase(it)` invalidates `it` but the for-loop does `++it`, causing undefined behavior and skipped entries.

findings.title: Metrics::errors_ never initialized
findings.description: `resolved_` and `created_` have default initializers but `errors_` does not, so `errors()` returns an indeterminate value.
